div.div: ARCHITECTURAL INVARIANT: SYNCHRONOUS RPC VS. ASYNCHRONOUS BROKER OBSERVABILITY

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 551px; margin-left: 48px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000; background-color: #FFFFFF;

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Comic Sans MS'; color: light-dark(#000000, #ededed); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; background-color: light-dark(#FFFFFF, #121212); white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
• Synchronous HTTP/gRPC: Thread-local storage (ThreadLocal/MDC) retains execution context naturally during blocking calls. Call stacks are contiguous.
• Asynchronous Event Broker: Execution thread terminates immediately upon broker publish acknowledgment. The receiving worker runs on an unrelated thread pool hours later.
• Consequence: Distributed tracing in message queues cannot rely on implicit runtime context. Context MUST be serialized into protocol headers (traceparent) at producer ingress and reconstituted at receiver egress. When consumers aggregate multiple messages in batches, standard single-parent hierarchy breaks, requiring W3C Span Links.
